skin.setting: a lighthouse on a sandbar in a winter storm, 1923
skin.title: The Light at Shingle Reef
skin.place: Shingle Reef Lighthouse, off the North Sea shoals
skin.styleGuide: Moody gouache illustrations with salt-crusted stone, lantern glow, churning dark seas, and vintage maritime workwear.

rooms.name: the North Vestibule
rooms.description: The drafty stone entry hall where heavy oilskin coats and iron wrenches hang by the iron door.

rooms.name: the Oil Store
rooms.description: A fortified chamber stacked high with kerosene drums and smelling sharply of paraffin.

rooms.name: the Foghorn Room
rooms.description: The low-ceilinged vault housing the pneumatic foghorn compressor and pressure gauges.

rooms.name: the Central Spiral
rooms.description: A narrow spiral staircase of perforated cast iron connecting the lower levels.

rooms.name: the Crew Quarters
rooms.description: The bunkroom and galley warmed by an iron potbelly stove and lit by a swinging lamp.

people.name: Elias Finch
people.bio: A taciturn veteran of the lighthouse service who has tended isolated beacons for fifteen years. He knows every bolt and oil valve in the station.
people.voice: Clipped and raspy, with the gruff brevity of a lifelong sailor.
people.motive: He was passed over for head keeper after the victim accused him of falsifying logbooks.
people.portrait: A weathered man in a patched wool sweater with a grey stubble beard and calloused hands.

people.name: Noah Vance
people.bio: Dispatched from the mainland to service the pneumatic siren before the winter storms set in. He spends most of his hours tinkering with machinery.
people.voice: Direct and hurried, speaking with oily hands tucked in apron pockets.
people.motive: The victim threatened to report his botched compressor repairs to the maritime board.
people.portrait: A wiry man in a smudged denim boiler suit and grease-stained flat cap.

people.name: Martha Crane
people.bio: A meteorological clerk stationed at the reef to record barometric data and gale patterns. Her methodical logs track the worst surges of the season.
people.voice: Quiet, precise, and measured, choosing each word with careful deliberation.
people.motive: The victim intended to burn her research notes after discovering she was reporting his neglect of duty.
people.portrait: A severe woman in a heavy tweed coat with round spectacles and an ink-stained ledger under her arm.

people.name: Captain Arthur Drake
people.bio: A tugboat captain marooned on the reef after his vessel broke its rudder on the shoals. He has been pacing the stone towers waiting for the gale to break.
people.voice: Booming and gravelly, accustomed to shouting over wind and churning waves.
people.motive: The victim failed to light the secondary beam, causing the wreck of Drake's tugboat.
people.portrait: A broad-shouldered captain in a brass-buttoned pea coat with tired, storm-reddened eyes.

people.name: Gregory Bell
people.bio: A strict and domineering superintendent who ran the beacon with an iron fist. His rigid management created friction with everyone confined on the rock.
people.portrait: A stern, unyielding man in an immaculate lighthouse service uniform with a scowl.

prose.c0: The coroner's assessment establishes that Gregory Bell was killed between nine o'clock and eleven o'clock.
prose.c85: "Noah Vance was not in the Crew Quarters at eight o'clock," said Captain Arthur Drake.
prose.c479: There was exactly one person in the Crew Quarters at ten o'clock.
prose.c20: Footstep records and iron grate latches confirm Elias Finch was not in the Central Spiral at nine o'clock.
prose.c278: A dropped brass button proves Captain Arthur Drake was in the North Vestibule at eleven o'clock.
prose.c411: Martha Crane was alone in the Crew Quarters at eight o'clock.
prose.c501: "I was with Noah Vance at eleven o'clock," said Martha Crane.
prose.c230: "Captain Arthur Drake was in the Foghorn Room at eight o'clock," Noah Vance stated.
prose.c171: "Martha Crane was not in the North Vestibule at nine o'clock," Noah Vance remarked.
prose.c114: Marks on the wet flagstones show that Noah Vance was not in the Foghorn Room at ten o'clock.
prose.c335: Logbook entries prove that Gregory Bell was not in the North Vestibule at ten o'clock.
prose.c497: Noah Vance and Martha Crane were both in the Crew Quarters at eleven o'clock.
prose.c599: "Gregory Bell was still alive at nine o'clock," insisted Elias Finch.
prose.c487: Elias Finch was alone in the Oil Store at eleven o'clock.
prose.c316: "Gregory Bell was not in the Central Spiral at eight o'clock," Captain Arthur Drake swore.
prose.c420: Not a soul was in the Oil Store at nine o'clock.
prose.c221: The dust across the floor grating indicates Martha Crane was not in the Oil Store at midnight.
prose.c565: Inspection of the scene confirms Martha Crane never set foot in the Foghorn Room.
prose.c527: Nobody was in the Central Spiral at midnight.
prose.c106: "Noah Vance was not in the Crew Quarters at nine o'clock," Captain Arthur Drake reported.
prose.c308: "Gregory Bell was not in the North Vestibule at eight o'clock," said Elias Finch.
prose.c219: "I was not in the North Vestibule at midnight," Martha Crane affirmed.
prose.c539: "Elias Finch was in the Oil Store at some point that evening," Noah Vance stated.
prose.c118: "Noah Vance was not in the Central Spiral at ten o'clock," Martha Crane noted.
prose.c40: "I was in the Oil Store at eleven o'clock," Elias Finch stated.
prose.c508: Captain Arthur Drake was alone in the North Vestibule at midnight.
prose.c520: "Somebody was in the Oil Store at midnight," Elias Finch recalled.

silence: "Nothing more to say about that hour. The storm is rattling the windows."
"Can't help you there, Inspector. I was minding my own duties."
"My records offer no observations regarding that matter."
"Haven't the foggiest notion, mate. Wind's too loud to hear anything."
skin.briefing: A ferocious blizzard has cut off Shingle Reef Lighthouse from the mainland, stranding four souls inside the stone tower alongside the body of Head Lightkeeper Gregory Bell. Found dead in the Foghorn Room, Bell met a violent end between the hours of eight o'clock and midnight. With the gale howling outside and escape impossible across the flooded sandbar, the killer remains inside.
skin.scene: A towering stone lighthouse battered by crashing ocean spray in a midnight blizzard, cold yellow light cutting through churning sea foam.
skin.summingUp:
Listen to the churning dark sea outside and look at how the lantern glow catches on these salt-crusted stones. Gregory Bell met his end right here in the Foghorn Room, and the timeline tells us exactly how it unfolded.

To begin with, the murder was not at eight o'clock or midnight, because Card 1 narrows down when the murder happened. Next, the murder was not at nine o'clock, because Card 5 has Gregory Bell still alive then.

That brings us to the later hours. The murder was not at eleven o'clock, because the killer and Gregory Bell were both in the Foghorn Room when it happened. That leaves ten o'clock as the exact hour Gregory Bell was struck down.

Finally, Elias Finch, Noah Vance and Martha Crane are in the clear, because the killer and Gregory Bell were both in the Foghorn Room when it happened. That leaves only one man with vengeance in his heart after the secondary beam was left unlit and his tugboat was wrecked on the rocks. The killer is Captain Arthur Drake.
